source_review.notes: Reviewed the original R-tree publication and Berkeley archive, official R*-tree record, and current SQLite/PostgreSQL R-tree/GiST documentation. All seven final destinations returned HTTP 200. Split, reinsertion, rounding, concurrency, and recovery claims remain scoped to the cited algorithm or implementation family.

evidence: Checked rectangle bounds, MBR, capacities M/m, area, enlargement, margin, overlap, dead space, candidates, reinsertion, condensation, and bulk loading.
Checked closed intersection, containment direction, exact geometry, and lossy candidate semantics remain distinct.
Checked page/tree balance terminology and root occupancy exceptions are explicit.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The chapter uses two-dimensional formulas while stating their coordinatewise higher-dimensional generalization.

evidence: Recomputed fixture four leaf MBRs, root (0,0,16,10), total leaf area 166, and pairwise overlap area 24.
Recomputed worked MBR area 35, insertion enlargement 14, and sibling overlap 16.
Recomputed exercise original area 20, new area 64, and enlargement 44.
Recomputed query (5,3,10,7) visits two leaves and matches C,D,F,K including boundary contact.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Area metrics use zero-area boundary overlap under ordinary measure while intersection semantics count touching.

evidence: Verified an MBR is formed by coordinatewise child minima and maxima.
Verified descendant enclosure plus parent-query disjointness implies no descendant match.
Verified area enlargement as area(union MBR)-area(existing MBR).
Verified split and condensation obligations preserve all-entry accounting, occupancy, and equal leaf depth.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Heuristic split quality is not represented as an optimality theorem.

evidence: Reviewed empty/root exceptions, edge touching, zero-area objects, duplicates, large objects, total overlap, high dimension, and skewed insertion orders.
Reviewed reversed bounds, NaN/infinity, float narrowing/outward rounding, CRS/dateline/geodesic semantics, and exact recheck.
Reviewed underfill, cascading splits/condensation, forced reinsertion loops, orphan entries/pages, stale parent MBRs, corrupt checksums, and overlap attacks.
Reviewed page latches, logical locks, reader restarts, WAL crash points, root publication, redo/undo, vacuum, and immutable segments.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The executable fixture excludes dynamic insertion/split/delete, floats, exact nonrectangular geometry, disk pages, concurrency, recovery, and adversarial overlap.

evidence: Static packing accounts for all 12 unique rectangle IDs in four leaves of exact capacity three.
Every rectangle is checked to be contained by its leaf MBR and all leaf MBRs by the computed root.
Inclusive query traversal prunes two of four leaves and exactly matches exhaustive rectangle intersection.
Exact fifteen-line output checks structure, areas, overlap, query visits, results, oracle agreement, and validity.
invariant_checking.notes: The model is a two-level static hierarchy, not a dynamic balanced R-tree.

evidence: Reviewed search correctness from ancestor enclosure through disjoint pruning and leaf exact recheck.
Reviewed insertion from choose-subtree through ancestor enlargement, overflow partition, parent propagation, and root growth.
Reviewed deletion from leaf removal through tightening, underflow reinsertion at the same level, and root shrink.
Reviewed crash-safe split from durable page creation and entry movement through logged parent/root publication and idempotent recovery.
proof_review.notes: No universal logarithmic search, optimal split, concrete database WAL, concurrency-control, or geospatial predicate proof is claimed.

evidence: Enclosure/pruning arguments are separated from heuristic area/overlap performance objectives.
MBR filtering is explicitly labeled candidate generation when true geometry is not rectangular.
The static executable model explicitly disclaims dynamic and storage-engine coverage.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Current implementation statements are attributed to SQLite/PostgreSQL documentation rather than generalized to every R-tree.

evidence: The standard-library Python model passed exact fifteen-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the repository verifier.
Independent arithmetic reproduced all MBR, area, enlargement, overlap, occupancy, and query values.
All seven final external destinations returned HTTP 200 and repository-local front-matter, sections, local links, examples, exercises, answers, and snippet checks passed before review.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No dynamic split/reinsertion/delete campaign, polygon/geography engine, float-rounding property test, page corruption, WAL crash/recovery, concurrency stress, I/O benchmark, spatial join, or production deployment was run.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter derives correctness from conservative enclosure and exact recheck while treating overlap, occupancy, split choice, and storage layout as performance and durability concerns.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed query operators/recheck, choose/split/reinsert/delete, quality metrics, bulk load, numeric/CRS semantics, page sizing, concurrency, WAL/recovery, corruption, validation, observability, and immutable-segment alternatives.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet contrasts R-tree overlap with k-d partitions; the model exposes MBR quality and pruning; ten examples cover enclosure, disjointness, enlargement, overlap, recheck, rounding, occupancy, roots, deletion, and crash recovery; five exercises transfer to migration and architecture.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/archive/official-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Guttman, Stonebraker, Beckmann, Kriegel, Schneider, Seeger, SQLite, PostgreSQL, database, storage, geospatial, concurrency, recovery, security, performance, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and model prove neither a production R/R*-tree or GiST operator class, optimal split, logarithmic query performance, exact geographic semantics, float-format safety, concurrent/WAL recovery protocol, certification, nor deployment fitness.
